articles.title: Joe Rogan renews multimillion-dollar podcast deal with Spotify
articles.summary: Spotify announced that it has renewed its deal with Joe Rogan, who heads the audio company's most popular podcast.
articles.body:
Spotify on Thursday said it had renewed its deal with Joe Rogan, who leads the audio company's most popular podcast, "The Joe Rogan Experience."

The podcast, which has 18 million followers on Spotify, has been the company's top podcast since 2020. The terms of the multiyear licensing deal were not disclosed. The Wall Street Journal , citing unnamed sources, reported the deal had an estimated earnout of $250 million.

"The partnership with Spotify has been an amazing fit, and they're incredible to work with," Rogan said in a statement. "I'm extremely happy and excited to continue with them for years to come."

Rogan first entered into an exclusive multiyear podcast deal with Spotify in 2020 in a deal said to be worth $100 million . The partnership was key to driving podcast audiences to Spotify, which at the time was mostly known as a streaming music service.

In 2024, the company extended its partnership for "The Joe Rogan Experience" to be distributed on other platforms, and that will continue in the latest deal. Rogan's show was ranked as the top podcast last year on Spotify, YouTube and Apple Podcasts.

"Joe has built something incredibly enduring, and his show continues to resonate with a massive global audience because there's simply nothing else like it," said Jordan Newman, head of content partnerships at Spotify, in a statement.

"The Joe Rogan Experience" has run into controversy, spurring a Spotify boycott in 2022 led by Neil Young over concerns that Rogan and his guests were spreading misinformation related to COVID-19 vaccines. Rogan also received criticism over his use of the N-word on past episodes of his show, for which he later apologized.

After the backlash, Spotify posted its content moderation rules and said it would add content advisory labels on COVID-related podcasts. Rogan also said he would do a better job of balancing different perspectives.

Young later returned to Spotify in 2024.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Braskem tem até esta sexta para avançar em acordo sobre dívida de R$ 56 bilhões; maior credor ainda não aderiu | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa, acionistas e credores tentam definir condições para reestruturar dívidas em recuperação extrajudicial. Braskem já tem apoio de 39,6% dos créditos envolvidos, mas precisa superar 50% até novembro para avançar com o plano.
articles.summary: A petroquímica precisa avançar nas negociações para reestruturar US$ 10,9 bilhões em dívidas; Banco de Nova York Mellon, com R$ 36,4 bilhões a receber, está entre os credores.
articles.body:
A Braskem tem até esta sexta-feira (9) para que seus principais acionistas e credores cheguem a um acordo sobre as condições comerciais do plano de recuperação extrajudicial da empresa, que prevê a renegociação de US$ 10,9 bilhões (R$ 56,5 bilhões) em dívidas.

A empresa, seus principais acionistas — Petrobras e FIP Shine I — e os credores que já aderiram ao processo precisam chegar a um consenso sobre os termos do plano. Segundo a Braskem, os termos da negociação estão em andamento e sendo discutidos entre as partes.

"A companhia permanece empenhada em buscar uma solução consensual e ordenada para sua reestruturação financeira e manterá o mercado informado sobre os próximos passos, no momento adequado", afirma a Braskem em nota ao g1.

Apesar de o prazo estar chegando ao fim, ele não encerra a recuperação extrajudicial. A Braskem ainda terá 90 dias, contados do protocolo do pedido, em 24 de agosto, para conquistar novas adesões e obter o apoio de mais de 50% dos credores abrangidos pelo processo. (saiba mais abaixo)

Ou seja, hoje é uma data decisiva para que a companhia avance nas negociações de sua dívida com os credores. Sem um acordo, há o risco de encerramento das tratativas, o que pode aumentar a pressão sobre a empresa e abrir caminho para um pedido de falência.

Já o prazo de 90 dias, que termina em meados de novembro, é o limite legal para que a Braskem obtenha o apoio necessário à aprovação de seu plano de recuperação extrajudicial.

Atualmente, os signatários representam 39,6% do total.

🔍 Na recuperação extrajudicial , a empresa negocia diretamente com seus credores uma forma de reorganizar as dívidas e depois leva o acordo à Justiça para homologação. É diferente da recuperação judicial , que envolve um processo mais amplo na Justiça. O acordo pode prever, por exemplo, mais prazo para pagar as dívidas ou um período sem pagamentos. Nos dois casos, o objetivo é evitar a falência e dar condições para que a empresa continue funcionando.

O que acontece se houver acordo nesta sexta-feira?

O acordo deve definir os princípios comerciais que vão orientar a elaboração da versão atualizada do plano de recuperação.

A proposta prevê a divisão dos sacrifícios financeiros entre os credores, a empresa e seus acionistas controladores.

Alterações nos prazos de pagamento das dívidas;

Períodos de carência para o pagamento do valor principal e dos juros;

Possíveis melhorias nas garantias e nas condições financeiras oferecidas aos credores.

O plano também prevê a possibilidade de converter parte da dívida em ações da companhia. Se isso ocorrer, a participação dos atuais acionistas poderá ser reduzida.

O pedido apresentado pela Braskem informa um passivo total de R$ 187,07 bilhões . No entanto, a maior parte desse valor não entra no cálculo da recuperação extrajudicial.

Desse total, R$ 130,6 bilhões correspondem a dívidas entre empresas do próprio grupo, chamadas de créditos intercompany. O valor representa cerca de 70% do passivo informado e foi excluído da base de cálculo do apoio dos credores.

A dívida efetivamente incluída na recuperação extrajudicial soma R$ 56,48 bilhões , o equivalente a US$ 10,9 bilhões em obrigações financeiras quirografárias.

🔎 A expressão significa, neste caso, dívidas financeiras que não contam com uma garantia específica sobre determinado bem. Nesse grupo estão títulos de dívida emitidos no exterior e contratos bancários.

Por que a Braskem entrou em recuperação extrajudicial?

A situação financeira da companhia foi pressionada por três fatores principais: os custos relacionados ao desastre geológico em Maceió (AL), as baixas margens no setor petroquímico global e o elevado endividamento financeiro.

O processo envolve seis empresas do grupo: a Braskem S.A. e cinco subsidiárias financeiras e operacionais no exterior.

A Justiça autorizou que as seis empresas sejam tratadas conjuntamente no processo. Essa estrutura, chamada de consolidação substancial, permite que os ativos e as dívidas das companhias sejam considerados em conjunto para determinados efeitos da recuperação.

A Braskem justificou o pedido pela gestão centralizada no Brasil, pelo controle comum das empresas, pela existência de garantias entre elas e pela atuação coordenada no mercado petroquímico.

A análise da NEOT Tecnologia, especializada em dados sobre recuperação judicial e insolvência, aponta essa questão como um dos pontos juridicamente mais vulneráveis do processo.

Segundo a avaliação, credores contrários ao processo podem questionar o cálculo conjunto das adesões, já que o percentual de 39,6% não é alcançado individualmente por todas as empresas, especialmente pelas subsidiárias no exterior.

A Braskem apresentou o pedido com o apoio de credores que representam R$ 22,38 bilhões, o equivalente a 39,6% dos créditos incluídos na recuperação.

Entre os signatários estão o Grupo Ad Hoc de Bondholders, formado por detentores de títulos de dívida emitidos no exterior, e instituições como Barclays Bank , Banco Santander , Citibank e Pentágono DTVM .

Os credores que ainda não aderiram representam os 60,4% restantes, equivalentes a cerca de R$ 34,09 bilhões. A Braskem precisa conquistar novas adesões para superar a maioria exigida por lei.

Entre as instituições que ainda podem aderir ao plano estão Itaú Unibanco , BNP Paribas , Crédit Agricole , Sumitomo Mitsui , Deutsche Bank , KfW IPEX-Bank , Natixis , Mizuho Bank , Bladex , DEG , DZ Bank , Standard Chartered Bank e Eco Securitizadora .

Os cinco maiores credores financeiros de mercado (excluindo intercompany):

The Bank of New York Mellon (BNY Mellon): R$ 36,44 bilhões (20,47% do total global)

Pentágono S.A. DTVM: R$ 2,24 bilhões (1,26% do total global)

Banco Santander S.A.: R$ 2,23 bilhões (1,25% do total global)

Barclays Bank PLC: R$ 1,80 bilhão (1,01% do total global)

Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC): R$ 1,11 bilhão (0,62% do total global)

Mesmo que as partes cheguem a um acordo sobre os princípios comerciais do plano nesta sexta-feira (9), a recuperação extrajudicial ainda terá outras etapas.

A Braskem tem 90 dias , contados do protocolo do pedido, em 24 de agosto, para obter o apoio de mais da metade dos créditos abrangidos pela recuperação. O prazo termina em 22 de novembro.

A versão atualizada do plano deverá ser apresentada à Justiça. Os credores poderão contestar a proposta, e a Braskem e as demais empresas envolvidas terão de responder aos questionamentos.

Na sequência, o Ministério Público analisará o processo antes de a Justiça decidir se homologa ou rejeita o plano.

Se a Braskem alcançar a maioria exigida e a Justiça homologar o plano, as condições aprovadas passarão a valer para todos os credores abrangidos, inclusive os que não aderiram à proposta.

Se a Braskem não obtiver a maioria necessária dentro dos 90 dias, a legislação permite que a empresa peça a conversão do processo em recuperação judicial.

articles.title: Trump cria comitê para investigar Lisa Cook, diretora do Fed, diz Casa Branca | G1
articles.standfirst: Comitê deverá apurar acusações contra a diretora do banco central americano e informar ao presidente se há justa causa para sua destituição.
articles.summary: Comitê deverá apurar acusações contra a diretora do banco central americano e informar ao presidente se há justa causa para sua destituição.
articles.body:
Montagem mostra Lisa Cook e Donald Trump — Foto: SAUL LOEB and ANDREW CABALLERO-REYNOLDS / AFP

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , anunciou a criação de um comitê para investigar Lisa Cook, diretora do Federal Reserve ( Fed ), o banco central americano, segundo um comunicado publicado no site da Casa Branca nesta sexta-feira (9).

“Para me auxiliar no cumprimento dessa responsabilidade, o comitê deverá investigar as acusações contra a diretora Cook e me informar se há ‘justa causa’ para sua destituição”, diz o comunicado, datado de 7 de outubro.

O comitê realizará uma audiência presencial na Casa Branca “para analisar as provas e as acusações contra a diretora”, segundo o memorando presidencial. O documento estabelece que a audiência terá duração máxima de quatro horas.

A criação do comitê é mais um passo na tentativa de Trump de retirar Cook do cargo . Trump já havia tentado demitir Cook em 2025 , acusando-a de cometer fraudes hipotecárias, o que ela nega.

A diretora, que é a primeira mulher negra a ocupar esse posto no Fed , afirmou que as acusações eram um pretexto de Trump para afastá-la do cargo por divergências sobre a condução da política monetária.

Em junho deste ano, a Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos bloqueou temporariamente sua demissão , por entender que o presidente não havia garantido a ela as condições previstas em lei para contestar as acusações.

Em agosto, a Casa Branca retomou a ofensiva e enviou uma carta à diretora, informando que Trump considerava afastá-la. O documento deu a Cook três semanas para responder as acusações. Na ocasião, seu advogado, Abbe D. Lowell, classificou as alegações como “sem fundamento” e afirmou que não havia causa válida para a demissão.

Ao barrar temporariamente a demissão, por 5 votos a 4, a Suprema Corte não analisou se as acusações eram verdadeiras. A decisão determinou que Cook deveria ter a oportunidade de se defender e devolveu o caso às instâncias inferiores da Justiça.

Cook foi nomeada para a diretoria do Fed em 2022 pelo então presidente Joe Biden, do Partido Democrata, e reconduzida em 2023 para um mandato que vai até 2038.

Desde a criação do banco central americano, em 1913, nenhum outro presidente havia tentado retirar um governador do Federal Reserve.

articles.title: Ibovespa opera em alta e vai aos 209 mil pontos, com inflação e eleições no foco; dólar cai | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana subiu 0,27%, cotada a R$ R$ 5,0242. Já a bolsa brasileira avançou 0,94%, aos 206.220 pontos.
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana subiu 0,27%, cotada a R$ R$ 5,0242. Já a bolsa brasileira avançou 0,94%, aos 206.220 pontos.
articles.body:
O dólar opera em queda nesta sexta-feira (9), com um recuo de 0,84% perto das 12h30, cotado a R$ 4,9822 . Já o Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, tinha alta de 1,41% no mesmo horário, aos 209.135 pontos .

▶️A inflação brasileira é o principal destaque da sessão. O indicador subiu 0,82% em setembro , após a deflação de 0,32% registrada no mês anterior. O avanço foi puxado principalmente por Habitação, por conta do fim do bônus de Itaipu nas contas de eletricidade, e por Transportes, com aumento das passagens aéreas e dos combustíveis. Na agenda internacional, dados de confiança do consumidor dos Estados Unidos ficam no radar.

▶️ No cenário eleitoral, novas pesquisas eleitorais indicaram vantagem de Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno. Segundo a pesquisa Datafolha, o candidato do PL deve ficar com 49% das intenções de voto no segundo turno, enquanto Lula (PT) deve ficar com 45%. Leia mais.

▶️ As incertezas sobre o conflito no Oriente Médio também continuam a influenciar os preços do petróleo no mercado internacional. Na véspera, Donald Trump afirmou que não atacaria o Irã antes das eleições de meio mandato, citando conversa "produtivas" com Teerã. Ainda assim, o bloqueio naval às exportações iranianas e os novos ataques a petroleiros no Estreito de Ormuz continuam a trazer dúvidas sobre a duração do conflito e sobre os impactos nos preços de energia globais.

Com isso, os preços do petróleo tinham volatilidade nesta sexta-feira. Perto das 12h30, o barril do Brent , referência internacional, subia 0,58%, cotado a US$ 104,89 . Já o West Texas Intermediate ( WTI ), referência dos EUA, avançava 0,47% , a US$ 91,92 o barril.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

A primeira pesquisa Datafolha do 2º turno mostra que Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tem 49% das intenções de voto, contra 45% de Lula (PT). O Datafolha diz que a distância de quatro pontos entre eles configura um empate técnico no limite da margem de erro, que é de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos, com maior probabilidade de Flávio Bolsonaro estar à frente.

Em votos válidos, Flávio Bolsonaro tem 52%, e Lula, 48%. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e pela Folha de S.Paulo.

A pesquisa também indicou que 49% dos eleitores desaprovam o governo do presidente Lula (PT), candidato à reeleição, enquanto 48% aprovam.

A pesquisa anterior, divulgada há uma semana, mostrava cenário idêntico: 49% desaprovavam e 48% aprovavam o governo.

O Datafolha ouviu 2.520 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 6 e 7 de outubro. A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O número de registro da pesquisa na Justiça Eleitoral é BR-0949/2026.

Nos Estados Unidos, os três principais índices de Wall Street operavam em alta nesta sexta-feira, de olho nos preços do petróleo e ações do setor de telecomunicações.

Perto das 12h30, o Dow Jones subia 0,50%, enquanto o S&P 500 avançava 0,43% e o Nasdaq Composite tinha alta de 0,46%.

Na Europa , o dia também era majoritariamente positivo. No mesmo horário, o DAX , da Alemanha, tinha ganhos de 1,20% e o CAC-40 , da França, subia 0,98%, enquanto o FTSE 100 , do Reino Unido, avançava 1,15%.

Na Ásia , os mercados fecharam mistos nesta sexta-feira, em uma semana de negócios reduzida por feriados em alguns dos principais índices acionários da região. Uma onda de vendas de ações relacionadas à inteligência artificial influenciou parte dos mercados da região.

O SSEC , índice de Xangai, subiu 0,05%, enquanto o CSI300 , índice que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em Xangai e Shenzen, avançou 0,16%. Entre os demais índices da região, o Nikkei , do Japão, recuou 0,02% e o Hang Seng , de Hong Kong, valorizou 1,79%.

O Kospi , da Coreia do Sul e o Taiex , de Taiwan, permaneceram fechados.

* Com informações da agência de notícias Reuters.

articles.title: Investors Pour Into Cash and Set to Stay, BofA’s Hartnett Says
articles.summary: Investors just poured money into cash funds at the fastest pace since the pandemic, and are unlikely to shift it anytime soon, according to Bank of America C...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Investors just poured money into cash funds at the fastest pace since the pandemic, and are unlikely to shift it anytime soon, according to Bank of America Corp.'s Michael Hartnett.

The large amount of cash on the sidelines is set to stay there until there is "big monetary easing" and sustained interest-rate cuts by the Federal Reserve, the strategist wrote in a note Friday. Money-market funds had inflows of $166.4 billion in the week ended Oct. 7, the most since April 2020.

"No rate cuts, no cash cuts," Hartnett wrote.

The bond market expects another three rate hikes in the US by the end of July, with the next expected at the December meeting. Large reductions in cash holdings tend to coincide with instances of big monetary easing, Harnett wrote.

Stocks face increasing competition from bonds and cash, safer investments with appealing yields, as interest rates rise globally in the face of inflation. Bonds saw a $33.8 billion inflow in the latest week, while $12.4 billion flowed into equities, according to BofA.

Hartnett views the US midterms as the most likely reason for a big move in stocks going into 2027, an event that he's taking a risk-off stance ahead given the current central-bank rate cycle and tighter financial conditions.

articles.title: Weight-loss drugs are hitting alcohol a lot harder than snacks, food-and-beverage VC explains
articles.summary: Weight-loss drugs may do more damage to booze than to the snack aisle, according to Nate Cooper, founder and managing partner of Barrel Ventures.
articles.body:
Weight-loss drugs may do more damage to booze shops than to the snack aisle, according to Nate Cooper, founder and managing partner of Barrel Ventures.

"At the end of the day, you have to eat, right? What you don't have to do is you don't have to drink alcohol," Cooper, whose first real check as an investor went into the nascent stages of Olipop, told Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi on the Power Players podcast (video above). "I think GLP-1s are having a much more severe impact on alcohol consumption than they are in food."

His reasoning: GLP-1 drugs "decrease addictive behaviors."

Sozzi noted that snacking giants such as PepsiCo ( PEP ), the owner of Frito-Lay, and Campbell's ( CPB ), the maker of Goldfish and Snyder's-Lance pretzels, are pushing back on the idea that GLP-1s will hurt their businesses over the long term.

Cooper expects "a slow drip effect" on snacking instead.

"Snacking is never going to disappear," he said, but brands will pack more protein and fiber into less food "because people are eating less."

What can replace alcohol if people drink less? Cooper's fund invested in Nowadays, a hemp THC beverage, a year and a half to two years ago. Cooper said Nowadays was the No. 2-selling item last year at the country's largest liquor retailer, behind a 750 ml bottle of Tito's vodka.

The appeal, he said, is "a similar feeling of having a drink or two without the downside effect of like waking up and feeling like crap in the morning."

Cooper said it's "not out of the realm of possibility" that the category could make up 10% of alcohol sales in stores, assuming it stays legal.

Extrapolated across US alcohol sales, he said, that would be $50 billion a year, for a category "that didn't exist five years ago."

He suggested a three-tier framework for lawmakers looking to regulate the drinks like alcohol: age-gate them, cap the milligrams, and "eliminate the synthetics."

articles.title: UPI vs credit cards: What should you choose for payments after MDR?
articles.summary: The author is CEO of Paisabazaar When it comes to choosing between UPI and credit cards, consumers should look at the overall value that they can derive
articles.body: The author is CEO of PaisabazaarWhen it comes to choosing between UPI and credit cards, consumers should look at the overall value that they can derive from each payment method rather than the immediate cost of the transaction. While UPI provides convenience and simplicity, credit cards offer cashback, rewards and additional perks. With MDR on higher-value UPI transactions now being discussed, understanding the complete economics of a transaction becomes even more important.The overall value of a transaction depends on several factors including the payment mode, transaction value, the applicable MDR (if any), and the value-back attached to the payment method. This becomes particularly relevant as UPI increasingly intersects with the credit card ecosystem through RuPay credit cards.UPI and cards serve different purposes in the consumer walletWhen a consumer makes a UPI payment from a bank account, the money is deducted directly from the account. While this offers simplicity and convenience, such payments generally do not come with any meaningful rewards, apart from occasional merchant-specific offers.A credit card changes this equation. The consumer can make the purchase today and get an interest-free period of 40-50 days, depending on the card's billing cycle and payment terms. Moreover, when it is a RuPay Credit Card that supports UPI payments, this flexibility is combined with the convenience of UPI.Value-back as rewards or cashback can change the economicsCredit cards are increasingly being designed around specific spending behaviours. Depending on the card, consumers can earn cashback or reward points on categories ranging from everyday purchases to high-ticket spends like travel bookings and electronics.Consider a Rs. 50,000 transaction on a card offering 5% cashback on the spend. The consumer could potentially receive Rs 2,500 back, subject to the card's terms, redemption value and applicable caps. Now if the consumer chooses to pay the same amount through UPI and the merchant passes on the entire MDR cost of 0.4% to the consumer, they will end up paying an additional Rs 200, making the product costlier for them, with no additional benefits.In fact, in most scenarios, credit cards can offer greater value to consumers through rewards, cashback and other benefits, without any additional payment processing charges being levied on them. However, this holds true only if consumers pay their credit card bills in full and on time, avoiding interest or finance charges. Once interest starts accruing on outstanding balances, it can outweigh the value earned through rewards or cashback, potentially nullifying the benefits of using a credit card.This is why comparing payment methods purely on the basis of transaction charges like MDR could be misleading. Rewards, offers and other value-back systems should also be taken into account. At the same time, a card may carry an annual or joining fee, impose reward caps, exclude certain categories, or offer a lower reward rate on certain transactions – which should also be considered.Transaction size alone does not determine the better choiceA common assumption is that UPI is best suited to small purchases while cards make more sense for larger transactions. However, in practice, the answer is more nuanced.Even a small Rs 500 transaction on a credit card could be more valuable than the same transaction through bank-account UPI if the card offers meaningful cashback or rewards on that particular spend. Conversely, a Rs 50,000 transaction may not necessarily justify the use of a credit card if the transaction falls outside the card's reward categories or has already exhausted the applicable monthly reward cap.Consumers should, therefore, look at the frequency of spending and the cumulative rewards generated over time. Small individual transactions can add up to significant value when they form a large portion of monthly expenditure. At the same time, card-specific discounts, cashback, merchant offers and reward points may add further value. Hence, the effective benefit can vary considerably across cards and merchants, irrespective of transaction values.Credit cards can offer value beyond the immediate transactionAn often-overlooked aspect of credit card payments is that their value is not limited to rewards. For consumers who manage their credit responsibly, the interest-free period can provide useful cash-flow flexibility. Some transactions may also be eligible for EMI conversion, allowing a large purchase to be spread across several months. Credit cards also come with issuer-specific offers, milestone benefits, travel privileges and more.But these benefits only have value when they are actually relevant to the consumer. Paying an annual fee for benefits that are rarely used does not necessarily make economic sense.The consumer's spending pattern should drive the choiceUltimately, there is no single payment method that will offer the best value for every consumer or every transaction. The important shift is to stop looking at payment methods only through the lens of convenience or transaction value and instead consider the net economics of the payment and choose the payment instrument that delivers the most meaningful value for one's individual spending pattern.MDR may change the equation, but not necessarily in the same way for everyoneThe discussion around MDR on higher-value UPI transactions adds another dimension to this comparison. MDR represents a cost associated with accepting a digital payment, and the relative economics for merchants can vary across payment instruments and transaction types.The impact on consumers, however, will depend on how the ecosystem responds. If merchants absorb the additional cost, there may be little or no visible impact on the consumer. If the cost is reflected in pricing or an additional payment-related charge, consumers may have to pay it as part of the product’s cost.Whether and to what extent merchants pass such costs on to consumers is yet to be seen.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Who would buy a home at today's mortgage rates?
articles.summary: Just 6% of homeowners and renters would take out a mortgage at today's rates.
articles.body:
Who wants to buy a home when mortgage rates are above 7%? The answer, unsurprisingly, is not many people.

The housing consulting firm John Burns Research & Consulting surveyed homeowners and renters about the highest rate they would accept on a mortgage. Just 6% said they would be willing to pay 7.5% to 7.99%, around today's current levels.

But if rates fell below 5.5%, nearly half of those surveyed would be willing to take out a mortgage. That level is something of a "magic mortgage rate" that market watchers believe would unleash a surge of new demand and bring sales out of their low-gear state. While rates never hit 5.5% this year, mortgage applications did pick up noticeably when rates were hovering around 6% earlier this year. And the latest rate rise has had a strong chilling effect on the market. Zillow found that pending home sales, which are recorded when a home goes under contract, were down 8.5% in September compared to a year earlier.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Video game hardware sales plunge to 13-year low as prices soar on memory, storage shortage
articles.summary: Video game console sales have plunged 13% on the memory and storage crisis.
articles.body:
The video game industry is taking a serious beating from the global memory and storage shortage. Microsoft ( MSFT ), Nintendo ( NTDOY ), and Sony ( SONY ) have all raised the prices on their respective consoles to offset both the increased component costs and the prior impact of tariffs.

And that has sent sales plummeting. According to data from market research group Circana, video game hardware sales for August fell 15% year over year to their lowest August totals in 13 years.

Take Sony's PlayStation 5, for example. A version of the console without a disc drive launched at $399 in November 2020. Today, it will cost you $599 . A version with a disc drive launched at $499 and now costs $649 . The high-powered PlayStation 5 Pro, which cost $699 when it debuted in 2024, is now priced at an eye-watering $899 .

Microsoft has made similar moves for its Xbox Series S and Series X. The S, which originally cost $299, is now $499, while the Series X climbed $250 to $749 .

Nintendo raised the price of the Switch 2 from $449 to $499 following President Trump's "Liberation Day" tariff increases last year.

According to Circana, video game hardware spending fell 3% in August, while year-to-date spending is down 11%.

"We are seeing the negative impact of those higher price points on the consoles. We're seeing a reduction in unit sales, driven by those higher prices," Circana executive director of games Mat Piscatella explained.

"We're also starting to see, spotty right now, but we're starting to see some products becoming unavailable, likely because of the RAM and component crisis," he added.

According to Piscatella, Sony's PlayStation 5 Pro, in particular, is extremely hard to find, with some retailers selling used versions of the console for more than $1,000, though it's unclear if that's directly related to the memory and storage shortage.

The big question, for Sony and Microsoft at least, is what all of this means for the launch of Take-Two Interactive's upcoming "Grand Theft Auto VI." One of the most anticipated media launches in history, "GTA VI" is expected to boost console sales among consumers who have held off on purchasing systems to date.

But higher prices could give some would-be buyers pause.

"The laggards of entering this generation, I bet a bunch of them are assuming that they're going to go to the store and pick [up a console] for $200, and instead it's going to be $600, $700, $800, $900 to try to pick up a console to play the thing," Piscatella said.

"I think there's going to be some sticker shock there if the consoles are even on the shelf to begin with," he said. "I'm sure there's going to be some kind of moderate [sales] boost, but there are so many factors at play."

Email Daniel Howley at dhowley@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on Twitter at @DanielHowley .

articles.title: Moderna stock jumps on planned national cancer vaccine effort
articles.summary: Moderna stock popped 9% on Friday after the New York Times reported new details about an effort to speed up cancer vaccine development. Investors saw the mRN...
articles.body:
Moderna ( MRNA ) stock popped 9% on Friday after the New York Times reported new details about an effort to accelerate cancer vaccine development. Investors saw the mRNA biotech company, in particular, as a beneficiary.

Other pharmaceutical stocks, including Pfizer ( PFE ), BioNTech ( BNTX ), and Merck ( MRK ), also rose.

According to the New York Times, the new initiative is a public-private partnership — similar to the effort that produced COVID-19 vaccines — that involves the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the NIH's nonprofit arm, researchers, pharmaceutical and biotech companies, advocacy groups, other nonprofits, and patients.

Stacey Adam, a senior clinical officer at the NIH's foundation, told the New York Times that she expects the program to launch in December. In 2024, the UK launched a similar program, called the Cancer Vaccine Launch Pad .

Moderna is viewed as a leader in mRNA cancer treatments. The stock soared in August on positive results for a melanoma treatment , developed with Merck.

This story is developing. Check back for updates.

articles.title: The AI SaaSpocalypse was supposed to crush software stocks — but this happened instead
articles.summary: Time to put this overused 2026 market slang to bed.
articles.body:
So much for the SaaSpocalypse eating all software stocks alive until they hit $0.

The overused 2026 market slang — which promoted the view that AI players like Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) would crush the business models of software-as-a-service companies — should be put to bed. Because after a stretch where this narrative hammered many software players, most have rallied sharply back.

The broader software group and the IGV index have rallied significantly since the end of June, JPMorgan strategist Samik Chatterjee pointed out (see the chart below), up 21% since the end of the month relative to the broader S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ), up 4%. Some of the top performers include Paycom ( PAYC ), DocuSign ( DOCU ), Workday ( WDAY ), Salesforce ( CRM ), Cloudflare ( NET ), Twilio ( TWLO ), and Microsoft ( MSFT ).

The broader rally has, in part, been helped by a valuation multiple rerating across infrastructure and application software companies, Chatterjee noted.

Renewed belief in software stocks could be sustained into year-end as investors digest third quarter earnings reports.

"Heading into C3Q earnings, we expect the broader share price momentum for the group to continue with infrastructure software companies leading the way on account of the AI-led tailwinds driving robust beats on both top-line and earnings, albeit potentially only in line on gross margins," Chatterjee said.

He added, "We expect application software companies to also participate in the positive share price momentum for the sector into the year-end on account of raises to full-year guides, aided by building momentum in AI monetization, which is steadily building as incremental revenue on top of the core businesses, which range from modestly decelerating to stable growth across our coverage companies."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. articles.title: She worked as a teacher till 62 years of age instead of retiring at 60, but was denied gratuity because of extended service; Allahabad HC orders payment with 6% interest
articles.summary: You work several years in an educational institution and are denied gratuity on the grounds that you worked beyond the retirement age. What do you do?
articles.body: You work several years in an educational institution and are denied gratuity on the grounds that you worked beyond the retirement age. What do you do? In one such case a retired teacher was denied gratuity and she challenged it in court.What the case is aboutA woman joined an educational institution in Faizabad as an assistant teacher on August 16, 1992. She continued working there until March 31, 2019, when she retired. However, the institution declined to pay her gratuity, arguing that the prescribed retirement age was 60 and she had remained in service until she was 62.On September 13, 2023, the Principal Secretary of the Uttar Pradesh Government's Minority Welfare Department rejected her claim for gratuity. The decision was based solely on the fact that she had continued working beyond the age of 60 and retired at 62.Also Read | Sisters sought share in parents’ properties under Hindu Succession law; Madras HC rules for brother over mother’s land on ouster, father’s estate over missing partiesThe retired teacher challenged the decision in court, arguing that working beyond the prescribed retirement age should not deprive her of gratuity. She pointed out that she had served the institution continuously for several years before retiring on March 31, 2019.Her challenge succeeded on September 30, 2026, when the Allahabad High Court directed the educational institution to pay her outstanding gratuity immediately, along with interest at 6% from 2019.Why did the retired teacher win the gratuity case?The Allahabad High Court noted that the state-regulated madrasa had refused to pay the woman’s gratuity by relying on government orders and rules, according to an ET report. According to the institution, she had failed to exercise her option to receive gratuity within the stipulated period.However, the court pointed out that she had been allowed to continue working until the age of 62 and had received all other retirement benefits admissible to her.The Allahabad High Court observed that merely citing the applicable government orders and alleging that the employee had not exercised the required option was insufficient to settle the question of her gratuity entitlement.Also Read | Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemptionThis was particularly relevant because the issue of denying gratuity on the basis of such an option had subsequently been examined authoritatively by both the Allahabad High Court and the Supreme Court, the report said.The court said that once the legal implications of allowing an employee to remain in service beyond the prescribed retirement age had been examined, and it had been held that such an extension could not, in the circumstances considered, justify denial of gratuity, the institution was required to assess the retired teacher’s claim in accordance with that legal position.The Allahabad High Court also referred to a Supreme Court judgment recognising gratuity as a beneficial scheme intended to protect eligible employees, reinforcing the principle that the benefit should be paid to those entitled to receive it.The Allahabad High Court observed that the teacher had been permitted to remain in service until March 31, 2019, when she turned 62, and had continued working accordingly. While settling her retirement benefits, the institution could not disregard the legal consequences arising from her extended service.Also Read | US-based daughter files case against parents seeking share in properties; Karnataka HC rejects her ‘ancestral’ claim, saying they were father's separate assets, not coparcenary propertyThe court further noted that the order rejecting her gratuity claim did not show that the institution had independently examined her entitlement to the benefit. Instead, the rejection rested on the allegation that she had not exercised the option to retire at the age of 60.Advocate Mayank Parashar of law firm Clasis Law explained to ET that Indian labour laws have traditionally placed employees' social security interests at the centre.Under both the new Labour Codes and the earlier legal framework, the circumstances in which gratuity can be denied are restricted. Continuing in employment beyond the retirement age with the employer's permission does not, by itself, constitute a valid ground for disqualification.According to Parashar, the retired woman succeeded because the reason cited for withholding her gratuity was not recognised as a legally valid ground under the applicable law.Although the judgment concerned an employee of a madrasa operating under state regulation, Parashar said its significance extends to establishments more broadly, including private-sector employers. The ruling underscores the need to assess gratuity claims properly before making a decision.Employers must have a clear and legally defensible reason before withholding or refusing gratuity or any other social security benefit, he added.The Allahabad High Court ruled in the retired teacher’s favour, entitling her to receive the outstanding gratuity along with interest at 6%.You use AI every day.
